text:
maria: Heads-up — seeing slow GPU/host memory growth + constant KV paging on qwen-mqa after we flipped kernel-selector to `opt-v2`. Long convo workloads (~50k tokens) eventually hit eviction thrash instead of stable reuse.

devin: Can you paste the short repro and the numbers? sounds like a fragmentation/regrowth loop. :thinking:

maria: repro command I used:```bash
python -m runtime.bench --model qwen-mqa --seq 51200 --kernel opt-v2 --batch 1 --profile kv --duration 30m
```

maria: sample KV telemetry (trimmed):
```
[00:05] tokens=51200 kv_entries=44800 kv_pages=280 host_alloc=12.1GB gpu_resident=9.4GB page_swaps=187
[00:10] tokens=51200 kv_entries=45200 kv_pages=284 host_alloc=13.9GB gpu_resident=9.5GB page_swaps=412
[00:15] tokens=51200 kv_entries=45240 kv_pages=288 host_alloc=15.6GB gpu_resident=9.6GB page_swaps=789
```

kevin: whoa, host_alloc jumping +2GB between samples while gpu_resident barely moves. looks like pages are being evicted to host and reallocated frequently. any change if you revert kernel?

maria: yep — rolled back to `opt-v1` on the same node: host_alloc stays flat ~11.9GB, page_swaps ~12 over same 30m. So regression tied to opt-v2 path.

rachel: my hypothesis: opt-v2 changed the internal page packing for MQA frames (different slot sizing) which increases fragmentation for Qwen's large head-size KV layout, especially when rope scaling toggles are on. small batches + bursty arrivals prevent compaction.

devin: that matches an earlier note about batch heuristics — if batcher creates many single-request micro-batches we never prime prefix cache and end up with extra transient pages. can you check batch distribution?

maria: distribution attached (summarized): 78% single-request batches, 18% 2-3, 4% >4. This test used `--batch 1` to mimic low-latency traffic; but production auto-batcher often still ends up with many singles because of kernel-perf scoring shift.

kevin: actionable: 1) reproduce with synthetic steady 4-request batching to see if fragmentation is alleviated; 2) add a quick guard in kernel-selector to prefer `opt-v1` for qwen-mqa when seq>32k; 3) run page-compact debug in staging to capture free list churn. assigning owners: kevin(1,2), rachel(3). :clipboard:

infra-bot: Started experiment job exp/kv-qwen-optv2-2026-03-18 at infra-run-42. Logs: http://ci.internal/exp/42 (will stream KV profile).

rachel: for the page-compact debug, add counters: free_chunk_count, largest_contig_pages, compaction_runs. if largest_contig_pages < target_slot then compaction should trigger.

maria: also noticed that rope scaling flag `rope_mode=adaptive` toggles mid-run for qwen-mqa depending on sequence statistical estimator; when it toggles we remap slots which forces more copies. suggestion: pin rope_mode for longer window during opt-v2 experiments.

devin: good catch. can you also dump KV slot metadata before/after a toggle? even a single sample will help confirm remap.

maria: will do and attach in the experiment run. putting a temporary rollback rule in config to use opt-v1 for qwen-mqa when seq>32768 until we complete analysis. :bug:

kevin: thanks — if experiment confirms, we should push a targeted kernel hotfix that preserves previous packing for MQA kernels or add a compaction pass after remap. low-risk hotfix first.

maria: note: this only repros reliably on machines with N=4 GPU pools where page eviction path uses host staging; tiny hosts with no swap behave differently. documenting infra variance in the run.

devin: milestone — get reproducer + full KV slot dumps in exp logs by EOD. ping me when uploaded.

maria: will do, thanks all. :thumbsup:
